text: PROBLEM.md records that Long and Wagner report a Gurobi check of their stronger Conjecture 5.2 for n <= 7. So f(7)=80 is almost certainly already known to them and this computation is an independent reproduction, not new mathematics. Do NOT claim novelty. Pinning down whether they state the value explicitly.

Reproduced decide_sat(7,80)=SAT independently: witness is exactly {v in Z_128 : v mod 8 in {1,3,4,5,7}}, size exactly 80, 0 excluded, cube-free under a from-scratch checker quantifying x,y,z over ALL of Z_128 and again via the Z_128->Z_8 quotient (T={1,3,4,5,7} has 0 cubes in 512 triples). The named worry is void: the definition demands x,y,z themselves lie in A, so looping over A is logically equivalent, confirmed on all subsets at n<=3 and 17k random at n<=5. Indexing and aux-var ranges checked; no collision. Both checkers reject all 48 single-element extensions, so neither is constant-True. Not breaks: claim never prints the witness, and --decide hardcodes ok=True regardless of witness_cubefree.

CONFIRMED that LW ran the computation, REFUTED that they state the value. LW Section 5 (arXiv v1, p.21, the only arXiv version): "Using Gurobi [12] we could check that for n <= 7 the following stronger conjecture is also true", then Conjecture 5.2: if S subset Z_2^n with |S| > (5/8)2^n then there exist x,y with Sigma*{x,x,x} subset S or Sigma*{x,3x,y} subset S. Both of those are 3-cubes, so 5.2 at n=7 gives f(7) <= 80; C_3 = L1 union L3 has size 2^(n-1)+2^(n-3) = 80 at n=7, so f(7) = 80 follows. DEFINITIONS MATCH claim-f7.md exactly: LW p.2 works "in the cyclic group Z_2^n", takes a multiset S of size d (not necessarily distinct), views Sigma*S as a set, and calls A d-cube-free iff no size-3 multiset has Sigma*S subset A. Degenerate triples are explicitly in scope (their example: Sigma*{2,5,5}). WHAT LW DO NOT DO: the number 80 never appears; no table of exact f(n); no per-n values, no model, no code, no certificate, no runtime; Conjecture 5.1 is stated as open and they claim no theorem at n=7. So the value is implied by their reported solver run, not published as a value. WIDER QUESTION: no exact f(n) for n >= 7 anywhere. Only 3 distinct works cite LW (Meng 2311.12318 / EJC 33(1) #P1.16, and Jing-Wu 2001.05632 / TAMS 10.1090/tran/8385); neither computes f(n). Meng p.5 still calls (5/8+o(1))N "conjectured by Long and Wagner", Tier 0 evidence the general bound is open. No OEIS entry for the sequence. LEAVES OPEN: an auditable, reproducible certificate for f(7) = 80, which LW give no artifact for, and the explicit statement of the value.

text: STRUCTURE, from the witness referee: the n=7 extremal set is {v : v mod 8 in {1,3,4,5,7}}, the preimage of T={1,3,4,5,7} under Z_128 -> Z_8. T is cube-free in Z_8 by exhaustion over all 512 triples. So |A| = 5 * 16 = 80 = 5/8 * 2^7, and the 5/8 constant is literally |T|/8. This is a third route to f(7) >= 80 with no solver, no cubes() and no is_cube_free.

text: CROSS-CHECK, two independent descriptions of the n=7 extremal set agree. Long-Wagner give the construction as a union of two layers of size 2^(n-1)+2^(n-3). The witness referee, working only from the SAT model, reported {v : v mod 8 in {1,3,4,5,7}}. Those are the same set: the four odd classes are the odd layer (64 elements) and the class 4 mod 8 is 4*odd (16 elements), totalling 80. The solver rediscovered the published construction without being told it.
